frontMatter.objective:
This manual outlines Gloster Limited's operational framework for managing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Our goal is to integrate sustainability and ethical governance into all business functions, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and stakeholder expectations.

The purpose of this ESG SOP manual is to:

Establish clear guidelines for managing environmental responsibilities, including waste minimization, water conservation, and air emissions control.
Promote social well-being through initiatives that enhance workplace safety, employee welfare, and community engagement.
Ensure governance excellence by implementing policies that safeguard financial integrity, protect customer data, and uphold transparency.
Drive continuous improvement in sustainability through innovation, monitoring, and regular policy reviews.

This document serves as a comprehensive resource to support our employees and stakeholders in achieving Gloster's ESG goals while fostering a culture of accountability and responsible business practices.
frontMatter.scope:
This SOP applies to all employees, subcontractors, stakeholders, internal and external customers, partners, vendors, regulatory bodies, the Board of Directors, and any other individual or entity associated with the Ananya unit of Gloster Limited.

Approved By: General Manager

sops.title: Workplace Safety Incident & Risk Management System

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the procedures for identifying, reporting, and managing workplace safety incidents, risks, and potential hazards at Gloster Limited. It is designed to ensure a safe and healthy work environment for all employees, minimize incidents through preventive actions, and foster a proactive culture of safety awareness across all facilities.

narrative.text:
Immediate Reporting: Any workplace safety incident or near-miss must be reported immediately by the employee involved to their immediate supervisor. This includes incidents such as slips, trips, falls, equipment malfunctions, or exposure to hazardous materials.
Use the designated reporting channels:
Email: safety@gloster.com
Incident Documentation: The supervisor must complete a Workplace Safety Incident Report Form with the following details:
Date and time of the incident
Location
Names of involved persons
Brief description of the incident
Immediate corrective actions taken
Initial Response: The supervisor is responsible for securing the incident area to prevent further harm. Immediate actions, such as administering first aid, evacuating the area, or shutting down equipment, are taken as needed.

sections.title: Health and Safety of Non-Employee and Contracted Workers

blocks.text: Gloster Limited ensures that non-employee and contracted workers operating on Company premises are provided with a safe and healthy working environment and are protected from occupational hazards.

Pre-Engagement Safety Requirements
Contractors and service providers must comply with Gloster Limited’s Health & Safety policies, site rules, and statutory safety requirements.
Prior to commencement of work, contractors shall submit relevant risk assessments, method statements, and worker competency details, as applicable.
High-risk activities are permitted only after approval through the Company’s permit-to-work system.
Safety Induction and Awareness
All non-employee and contracted workers must undergo a mandatory site safety induction before accessing operational areas.
The induction covers:
Site-specific hazards
Emergency procedures and evacuation routes
PPE requirements
Incident and near-miss reporting procedures
Supervision and Safe Work Practices
Contracted activities are carried out under designated supervision by authorized Gloster personnel.
Supervisors ensure compliance with approved safe work practices and immediate correction of unsafe behaviors.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Appropriate PPE is mandatory for all non-employee workers based on task-specific risks.
Compliance with PPE requirements is monitored throughout the work period.
Incident Reporting and Emergency Response
All safety incidents, injuries, near misses, or unsafe conditions involving non-employee or contract workers must be reported immediately through the same reporting channels as employees.
Non-employee workers are included in emergency response procedures, including evacuation, first aid, and medical assistance.

body.text:
Conducting Risk Assessments:
Annual risk assessments must be conducted across all Gloster facilities. This includes evaluating the safety of equipment, tools, materials, and working conditions.
Each work area will maintain a Risk Register where identified risks are documented, including their nature, likelihood, impact, and control measures.
Risk Control Measures:
Engineering Controls: Modify equipment or add barriers to mitigate risks.
Administrative Controls: Implement new safety protocols and rules.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Ensure the use of gloves, masks, and safety goggles.

Incident Investigation Team: A team comprising members of the Safety Committee and supervisors relevant to the incident area will investigate all reported incidents.
Root Cause Analysis:
The investigation team will perform RCA to determine the underlying causes of the incident.
Findings from RCA are documented, along with recommendations for Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) to avoid recurrence.

blocks.text:
Mandatory Safety Training: All new employees undergo onboarding safety training covering hazard identification, safe work practices, emergency responses, and proper equipment usage. Refresher courses are provided annually and following any major incident or policy update.
Record-Keeping:
Training attendance and assessment results are documented and maintained by the Training & Development Department.

responsibilities: Report incidents immediately, follow all safety protocols, participate in safety training sessions.
Document incidents, secure the area, report to Safety Officer, conduct routine inspections.
Assess reported incidents, manage risk assessments, coordinate safety training, and maintain records.
Review and approve safety protocols, ensure sufficient resources, support safety initiatives.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed by the Health & Safety Manager every two years or following any significant incident. Revisions are made to ensure ongoing compliance with regulatory standards and workplace safety practices.

sops.title: Sustainable Product Recovery and Disposal Strategy

blocks.text: This SOP outlines Gloster Limited’s sustainable product recovery and disposal strategy, aimed at reducing waste, minimizing environmental impact, and promoting responsible disposal practices throughout the product lifecycle. This approach aligns with Gloster’s commitment to sustainable practices and community welfare.
Design Principles:
Design Aimed at Reducing Resource Input:

At Gloster Limited, sustainable design is at the forefront of our product development process, aimed at minimizing resource input and maximizing efficiency. Our strategies include:
Material Efficiency:
In the design phase, product teams are required to prioritize materials that minimize environmental impact, specifically those that reduce energy and water consumption during production.
This involves a careful selection process where sustainably sourced materials are given precedence. Recycled or upcycled materials should be incorporated whenever feasible, contributing directly to Gloster’s goal of fostering a circular economy.
Each product should meet a minimum threshold of 25% recycled content, and records of material sources and recycled content percentages are to be maintained for every product line.
Annual audits will evaluate our compliance with these standards and assess any updates needed to meet emerging sustainability goals.
This approach not only enhances environmental responsibility but also strengthens our brand's commitment to reducing its carbon footprint.
Durable Construction:
All products must be designed for longevity, ensuring they withstand rigorous use and reduce the need for frequent replacements, which lowers additional resource consumption over time.
The design team conducts standardized durability assessments on each product, testing for wear resistance, structural integrity, and suitability for long-term use.
Products are expected to meet high durability standards prior to market release, ensuring they align with Gloster’s reputation for quality.
To reinforce these standards, an annual review of durability benchmarks will be conducted, with updates implemented as necessary to keep pace with industry advancements.
Documentation of testing outcomes is required, and any material adjustments should be recorded to maintain compliance with Gloster’s durability protocols.
Furthermore, feedback from end-users will be incorporated into future designs to enhance durability based on real-world use.
Waste Minimization and Low-Impact Dyeing Processes:

To further reduce resource input, excess materials from production, including offcuts and remnants, are to be repurposed or recycled whenever possible.
Offcuts may be used in the creation of labels, smaller components, or secondary product lines, promoting resource efficiency. Additionally, all dyeing processes should prioritize the use of low-impact dyes that require minimal water and energy, reducing the environmental burden.
Dyeing standards will be evaluated quarterly to ensure they meet Gloster’s sustainability targets, with adjustments made as new, lower-impact technologies become available. All waste reduction practices must be recorded and reviewed biannually to identify areas for improvement and maximize resource efficiency.
These protocols support our commitment to minimizing environmental impact throughout the production lifecycle.
Reducing Microfiber Release and Fabric Fraying:

Understanding the environmental impact of microfibers, Gloster Limited takes proactive measures to minimize shedding and tearing through:
Innovative Fabric Choices:
Our product teams prioritize fabric technologies that reduce microfiber shedding during normal use and washing cycles, directly addressing the issue of microplastic pollution. Research teams actively collaborate with jute manufacturers to identify and test fabrics with low-shed properties, ensuring they meet both durability and environmental standards.
Eco-friendly fabric treatments are also explored to enhance material resilience while preserving comfort and softness. Each fabric undergoes testing to verify that it aligns with Gloster’s sustainability targets, and records of each material’s performance are maintained for ongoing evaluation.
Additionally, Gloster is committed to working with suppliers to adopt treatments that improve fabric durability without compromising on texture or aesthetic quality, helping to create a product that is both eco-friendly and user-friendly.
Robust Design:
To enhance durability and further reduce shedding, products are designed with reinforced seams and construction techniques that mitigate stress points prone to tearing.
Gloster’s design teams incorporate reinforced stitching and structural elements in areas that typically endure high stress, such as hems, cuffs, and pockets, which supports product longevity. Feedback from users on product wear-and-tear is systematically collected and reviewed during the design process, allowing for continuous improvements that reflect real-world usage.
Testing on resilience is performed as part of our standard quality control, ensuring that each product adheres to durability standards. Design adjustments are logged and reviewed quarterly to keep pace with innovation and maintain product quality, fostering a robust and eco-friendly design approach.
Information on Efficient Use, Storage, and Maintenance:

Gloster Limited is committed to empowering customers with comprehensive guidance on the efficient use, storage, and maintenance of its products. This initiative aims to extend the product life cycle and minimize environmental impact. Key recommendations include:
Proper Storage Techniques:
We advise customers to store jute products in a cool, dry environment, away from direct sunlight and temperature extremes. For example, a retail store stores their jute bags in climate-controlled rooms, helping preserve durability and prevent material degradation caused by UV light and fluctuating temperatures.
To avoid moisture accumulation, we recommend using breathable storage solutions like cotton bags or mesh containers. A customer found that using breathable storage helped significantly reduce mold formation on their stored goods, keeping their products in better condition for longer.
We suggest customers use temperature and humidity monitors to maintain optimal storage conditions. A customer added these devices to their storage areas, which helped them maintain consistent conditions and reduced instances of mildew and fiber deterioration.
Store products in well-organized spaces to ensure proper air circulation. A customer who reorganized their warehouse reported improved airflow around their products, minimizing the risk of material degradation.
Maintenance Practices:
For cleaning jute products, we recommend cold water washing and air drying to avoid weakening fibers. A local store follows this practice and has noticed a marked improvement in product lifespan, reducing wear and tear significantly.
We also suggest performing regular inspections for any signs of wear. A customer checks their jute bags every six months for fraying or stitching issues, which has helped prevent major damage and extend the life of their products
If minor damage occurs, we recommend customers use jute thread for stitching up small tears. A customer successfully repaired a small tear in a jute bag this way, preventing the issue from worsening and prolonging the product’s usability.
We advise customers to avoid harsh cleaning agents, which can weaken the fibers. A business switched from chemical cleaners to natural soap-based solutions, significantly improving the longevity of their jute products.
Usage Tips:
We encourage customers to observe load limits to avoid overstretching jute products. For example, a company that uses jute sacks for transporting goods limits each sack to 50 kg, ensuring the material doesn't tear prematurely.
Customers should handle products gently to avoid rough abrasion. A customer who switched to gentler handling practices reported fewer product damages, leading to increased satisfaction.
We recommend that customers carefully handle jute products during transport to avoid damage from friction or impact. A customer who implemented this tip saw a decrease in product damages during shipment.
We suggest customers avoid overloading bags or sacks, as this can stress the fibers and reduce the product’s lifespan. A local company reports using lighter loads has resulted in longer-lasting jute products.
Customer Access to Product Care Information: Comprehensive guidance on storage, maintenance, and usage recommendations is available on our website and in product brochures. Customers can easily access practical tips on extending product lifespan and minimizing environmental impact.
Return Programs:

Collection Points:
Gloster Limited provides designated collection points for returning end-of-life products. Users can return products at the following locations:

Collection Hours: Monday to Saturday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM

Return programs are designed to be convenient, with clear instructions provided on how and where to return products. Customers may also return products through mail-in options, which are detailed on the company’s website: https://www.glosterjute.com/about.
For any query or guidance contact following person:

Contact Number: +91 9874820561
Recycling Facilities:
Users are provided with detailed information on local recycling facilities capable of processing specific product types. This includes contact information, addresses, and guidelines on how to prepare products for recycling:
Bansberia Recycling Facility
Facility Type: Certified for textile recycling
Kolkata Recycling Hub
Facility Type: General recycling
Gloster Limited collaborates with these certified recycling partners to ensure that materials are processed in an environmentally friendly manner and that recycling practices are compliant with sustainability standards.
Sanitary Waste Management:
For products that cannot be recycled, Gloster Limited offers guidance on appropriate sanitary waste management practices. This includes:
Contact details for local waste management authorities and facilities.
Instructions on safe disposal methods to prevent contamination and environmental harm.
Local Waste Management Authority
Disposal Methods: Regular collection and safe handling guidelines. Contact: West Bengal Waste Authority, Phone: 040 2444 6000.
Environmental Impact Minimization:
Environmental Manager

Impact assessment: Gloster Limited is committed to continuously assessing the environmental impact of its products throughout their lifecycle. Our environmental impact assessments evaluate factors such as energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, resource usage, waste generation, and the toxicity of materials used. We also examine water usage, pollution risks, and effects on biodiversity, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations. This ongoing process allows us to monitor the effects of product design, manufacturing, usage, and disposal, helping us identify areas for improvement and make informed decisions to reduce our environmental footprint, enhance sustainability, and minimize negative impacts on ecosystems and human health.
Waste to Landfill: Gloster Limited aims to reduce the amount of waste sent to landfill by promoting recycling and reusing materials wherever possible. Employees are encouraged to segregate waste into recyclable, compostable, and non-recyclable categories to streamline waste processing and ensure that reusable materials are utilized effectively.
Leakage Prevention: Users are advised on how to prevent product component or residue leakage during disposal, especially for products that contain materials that could harm the environment. Proper storage and handling procedures will be introduced to prevent leaks, and all employees will be trained to handle hazardous materials safely, ensuring that waste disposal complies with environmental regulations.
Virgin Material Use Reduction: The company encourages the reuse of product components to minimize the need for virgin materials in the production of new products. This includes utilizing materials from returned or recycled products and sourcing from suppliers that prioritize sustainable practices. The company also promotes using alternative, sustainable raw materials wherever possible to reduce the environmental footprint.
Proper Disposal of Products to Promote Circular Material Flow:

Gloster Limited actively encourages customers to return used products through our designated collection points or mail-in options, contributing to the promotion of a circular material flow. In collaboration with certified recycling agencies, we ensure that products returned at the end of their lifecycle are properly processed. By recycling these products, valuable materials are reclaimed and reintroduced into the production process, reducing the need for virgin resources and decreasing waste sent to landfills. This approach not only helps conserve natural resources but also supports the transition to a more sustainable, circular economy.
Packaging Optimization
Design Principles:

Material Reduction (Lightweighting): Our team has redesigned product packaging for our skincare line to use thinner but durable materials. By reducing the thickness of plastic bottles, we’ve created lighter packages that require less energy during transport and produce less waste.
These lightweight packages maintain high standards for product protection while minimizing material use.
Monomaterial Packaging: Our beverage cartons now use a single type of material, such as polyethylene. By removing mixed materials, these packages can now be fully recycled through standard plastic recycling channels, reducing their environmental footprint.
This shift simplifies the recycling process for consumers and supports our commitment to enhanced recyclability.
User-Friendly Recycling: Our packaging now includes clear, visual recycling instructions. For instance, snack wrappers display a “tear here” line along with recycling icons and simple text, guiding customers to separate plastic films from cardboard inserts.
We also provide a QR code on our packaging that links to an instructional video, helping customers understand how to prepare the packaging for recycling effectively.
Implementation Strategies:

Product Design Integration: During the design of our new line of eco-friendly jute bags, our team focused on selecting sustainable materials and packaging that would be easy to recycle. The design incorporated minimal packaging, using biodegradable labels and paper-based adhesives to ensure the packaging could be recycled alongside the product.
Additionally, the design of the jute bags took into consideration how the packaging could be reused for other purposes, further reducing waste.
Design for Easy Disassembling, Remanufacturing, or Recycling of Jute Products: For our jute-based products, we incorporated design elements that facilitate easy disassembly for recycling. Jute fibers are stitched together with biodegradable cotton threads, allowing the bags to be easily disassembled at the end of their life cycle.
Furthermore, the jute products are designed for remanufacturing, where the jute material can be upcycled into new products, reducing waste and extending the life of the raw materials.
We collaborated with recycling partners to ensure the end-of-life process for our jute products is as sustainable as possible, reducing the environmental footprint of both the product and its packaging.
Continuous Improvement: The company regularly reviews packaging designs to identify opportunities for further reduction in material use and improvements in recyclability.
Exclusions:

The SOP does not cover secondary and tertiary packaging, such as protective shrink wrap, foam reinforcement, crates, and pallets used for shipping and bulk transportation. Focus remains on primary packaging that comes into direct contact with the product.

This SOP provides a structured response for managing IT security incidents at Gloster Limited. It is designed to prevent data breaches, minimize the impact of cyber threats, and maintain the security of Gloster’s information systems, supporting the company’s ethical standards and governance philosophy.

body.text: Detection and Immediate Reporting:
Initial Detection: Employees are required to report any suspicious activity or potential security breaches within 1 hour of discovery.
Designated Reporting Channels:

Email: itsecurity@gloster.com
Emergency Contact: Mr. Abhishek Sharma, Phone: +91 98748 20561
Required Details: Reports must include the incident date, time, system(s) affected, description of suspicious activity, and initial threat level assessment.

Immediate Actions: The IT Security Team takes containment actions, such as isolating affected systems, revoking access rights, or temporarily disabling network services, to prevent further compromise.
Documentation: All actions taken to contain the incident are recorded in the Incident Response Log with specific timestamps and responsible personnel.
Assessment of Incident: Within 24 hours of containment, the Data Protection Team, in collaboration with the IT Security Team, assesses the incident’s scope, potential impact, and root causes.
Root Cause Analysis (RCA): The team performs RCA to identify vulnerabilities and determine appropriate corrective and preventive measures (CAPA).

Decision to Notify: If a data breach impacts customer or employee data, the IT Security Manager, in consultation with Gloster’s Legal Department, determines if notification to authorities or affected individuals is required.

Notification Details: Notifications include information on the nature of the breach, data affected, and steps taken to mitigate the impact. Communication is consistent and transparent to reassure stakeholders.

CAPAs Implementation: Corrective Actions: Immediate measures are taken to rectify vulnerabilities. Preventive Actions: Long-term measures, such as updated access protocols or enhanced firewalls, are implemented to prevent recurrence.
Incident Log Maintenance: The Incident Response Log, containing details of all actions taken and personnel involved, is maintained for compliance and future reference.
Post-Incident Review: The IT Security Team conducts a review to identify lessons learned, update the Incident Handling SOP, and document improvements for future incidents.

responsibilities: Detect, respond to, and document IT security incidents.
Lead breach assessment and manage external notifications.
Report incidents and adhere to IT security guidelines.
Advises on regulatory compliance and legal requirements for breach notification.

sops.title: Authorization & Approval Process for Critical Transactions
sops.owner: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Compliance Officer

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the approval process for critical transactions, such as high-value purchases, gifts, and travel expenses, to uphold Gloster Limited’s ethical standards and mitigate financial risks. It ensures compliance with company policies and prevents conflicts of interest.

Sensitive transactions under this SOP include discretionary interactions involving external stakeholders, such as suppliers, customers, consultants, agents, service providers, and government or regulatory representatives, where there is, or may be perceived to be, a personal benefit in addition to a legitimate business purpose.

These transactions may occur in the context of gifts, hospitality, travel, meals, accommodation, or appreciation of professional services and carry an inherently higher risk of improper influence or corruption.

rows.definition: Includes transactions such as gifts, travel, and other benefits that could create a conflict of interest.
Designated individuals or departments responsible for reviewing and approving sensitive transactions.
Any situation where a reasonable third party may perceive a transaction as providing a personal advantage, favor, or improper influence, even if no actual benefit was intended or received.

substeps.text: All sensitive transactions must be identified and documented. Examples include gifts exceeding a specified monetary threshold, business travel for non-routine purposes, or other benefits.
Thresholds: Gifts or benefits valued above ₹5,000 and travel expenses above ₹25,000 require specific approval.
Prohibited and Restricted Transactions: Cash, cash equivalents, gift cards, vouchers, or personal loans are strictly prohibited.
Sensitive transactions must not influence, or appear to influence, business decisions.
Repeated or frequent gifts or hospitality to or from the same external stakeholder require enhanced scrutiny and senior management approval.
Any offer received that exceeds defined thresholds or creates discomfort must be reported even if declined.

Documentation: Complete a Sensitive Transaction Request Form for each transaction. This form should include: Name of the recipient; Description of the transaction (gift, travel, etc.); Monetary value; Purpose of the transaction; Date and location; Justification for the transaction and any supporting documentation (e.g., travel itineraries, invoices).

body.text: Submit the completed Sensitive Transaction Request Form to the immediate supervisor or department head for an initial review. The supervisor will evaluate the transaction for compliance with company policies and potential conflicts of interest.

Transactions requiring approval should be submitted to the following authorities based on the value. Gifts: Above ₹5,000: Department Head; Above ₹10,000: Senior Management. Travel Expenses: Above ₹25,000: Senior Management; Above ₹50,000: Executive Committee.

The approving authority will review the documentation and justification provided. They may request additional information if needed. Approval or rejection of the transaction must be documented in writing, including reasons for approval or denial.

Processing: Once approved, process the transaction according to company procedures. Ensure that all documentation is complete and accurate. For travel expenses, ensure that travel arrangements are booked in accordance with company travel policies.

Recording: Maintain a record of all sensitive transactions, including approvals, supporting documentation, and any related correspondence. Records should be retained for a minimum of 5 years and made available for audit or review as needed.

Conduct annual reviews of sensitive transactions to ensure compliance with policies and identify any potential issues or patterns. Offers of gifts, hospitality, or benefits received from external stakeholders, whether accepted or declined, are reviewed periodically to identify patterns or potential risks. Review findings should be documented and reported to the relevant authorities for further action if required.

responsibilities: Document and submit all sensitive transactions for approval.
Conduct initial review, ensure compliance, and provide recommendations.
Maintain transaction records, conduct periodic reviews, and ensure adherence to ethical standards.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed by the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Compliance Officer every two years to ensure it aligns with regulatory requirements and Gloster’s internal ethical policies.

sops.title: Data Access Control & Customer Data Management Framework

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the internal controls and procedures implemented by Gloster Limited’s to restrict unauthorized access to customer or client data, both physical and digital. It also provides guidelines on consulting and informing customers about the collection, storage, and sharing of their personal data.

rows.definition: Personal and sensitive information collected from customers or clients, including names, addresses, contact details, payment information, and any other data shared during transactions.
Access to data by individuals or entities not explicitly granted permission to view, modify, or use the data.
A timetable that specifies the duration for which different categories of data are kept and the actions to be taken at the end of the retention period.

body.text: Restricted Areas: Customer data is stored in secured areas accessible only to authorized personnel. Access to these areas requires security clearance and is monitored by CCTV. For example, physical copies of purchase orders and invoices containing customer addresses and payment details are kept in locked cabinets within a secured room.

Document Handling: Physical documents containing customer data must be stored in locked cabinets or rooms with restricted access. Employees must sign in and out when accessing these documents. Sensitive documents like contracts, legal agreements, and customer identification proofs are strictly controlled and logged.

User Authentication: All employees accessing digital data systems must use unique user IDs and strong passwords. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced for sensitive data access. For instance, employees must enter a password and a one-time code sent to their mobile device to access the customer database.

Access Permissions: Data access permissions are granted based on job roles and responsibilities. Employees only have access to the data necessary for their tasks. Regular audits are conducted to ensure compliance. For example, only the finance team can access customer payment details, while the sales team can view contact information and order history.

Data Encryption: Sensitive customer data is encrypted both in transit and at rest. Encryption keys are securely stored and managed. Emails containing customer details are encrypted before sending, and databases storing personal information are protected with strong encryption algorithms.

Third-Party Access: Access to customer data by third-party vendors or service providers is restricted and granted only when necessary. Contracts include clauses ensuring data protection compliance. For example, a third-party logistics provider is given access only to customer shipping addresses for order fulfilment.

Activity Logs: All access to customer data is logged, including the date, time, and user involved. Logs are regularly reviewed for any unauthorized access attempts. If a breach attempt is detected, an alert is immediately sent to the IT security team.

Regular Audits: Data access controls are subject to regular internal audits to identify vulnerabilities and ensure adherence to this SOP. Audits include reviewing access logs, verifying encryption standards, and assessing third-party compliance.
Data Collection Notice:

Transparency: Customers are informed about the types of data being collected, the purpose of collection, and how it will be used at the time of data collection. For example, customers are notified that their contact information is collected for order processing and delivery notifications.

Consent: Explicit consent is obtained from customers before collecting their personal data, especially for sensitive information. Customers have the right to opt out of data collection where applicable. For instance, consent is required to collect and store customer bank account details for payment processing
Data Storage and Sharing Information:
Data Retention: Customers are informed about the duration for which their data will be stored and the criteria used to determine this period.

Third-Party Sharing: If customer data is shared with third parties (e.g., for shipping or payment processing), customers are informed of the entities involved and the purpose of sharing. Third-party partners are vetted to ensure they comply with data protection standards. For example, shipping addresses are shared with logistics providers solely for the purpose of order delivery.
Customer Consultation and Queries:

Access Requests: Customers have the right to request access to their data, request corrections, or ask for their data to be deleted. These requests are handled promptly and in accordance with data protection laws. For instance, a customer can request the deletion of their account and all associated personal information if they decide to stop using the company's services.
Communication Channels: Customers can contact the company via email: info@glosterjute.com or Tel: +913322309601 for any queries regarding their personal data.
Data Breach Notification:

Immediate Notification: In the event of a data breach that compromises customer data, affected customers are notified promptly. The notification includes details of the breach, the data affected, and the steps being taken to mitigate the impact. For example, if unauthorized access to customer email addresses is detected, the company will notify all affected customers and advise them on how to secure their accounts.
Follow-up Support: The company provides support to customers following a breach, including offering credit monitoring services or guidance on securing their personal information.

Prior to collecting any personal or confidential information, Gloster Limited ensures that customers or clients are clearly informed about:
The type of data being collected (e.g., contact details, payment information, order history)
The purpose of data collection
The duration of data retention
Whether the data will be shared with third parties and for what purpose
Consent is obtained through one or more of the following mechanisms:
Signed physical consent forms
Digital consent checkboxes on websites or portals
Consent clauses embedded in contracts, quotations, or service agreements
Email-based consent confirmations for remote transactions
Consent requests are presented in clear, simple language and are obtained before any data is processed or stored.

steps.heading: Consent for Data Sharing with Third Parties

body.text: Where customer or client data is required to be shared with third parties (such as logistics partners, payment processors, IT service providers), separate and explicit consent is obtained. Customers are informed of: The name or category of third parties; The specific data elements being shared; The purpose and duration of such data sharing. Data sharing is strictly limited to the minimum information necessary to perform the intended service.

All consent records are: Logged electronically or physically; Linked to the relevant customer or transaction; Retained for a minimum of five (5) years or as required by applicable law. Consent records are made available for internal audits, external audits, and regulatory inspections.

Customers and clients have the right to: Withdraw consent; Modify previously given consent; Request restriction of data processing. Consent withdrawal requests can be submitted via: Email: info@glosterjute.com; Written request to the registered office. Upon withdrawal of consent: Data processing is stopped unless legally required; Data is securely deleted or anonymized as per the Data Retention Schedule.

Consent validity is reviewed periodically, especially when: The purpose of data use changes; New third parties are introduced; Retention periods are extended. Fresh consent is obtained wherever required.

responsibilities: Implements data protection controls, manages audits, and ensures compliance with data protection laws.
Adhere to data access protocols and report unauthorized access immediately.

This SOP outlines the measures and technologies implemented by Gloster Limited to prevent and control air pollution within its textile manufacturing processes. It aligns with Gloster’s mission to reduce environmental impact, meet compliance standards, enhance sustainability practices, and ensure the health and safety of employees and surrounding communities.

body.text:
Routine Monitoring: Gloster Limited conducts quarterly ambient air monitoring for PM10, PM2.5, SO2, and NOx to assess environmental impact and identify areas for improvement.
Preventive Maintenance: Regular inspections and preventive maintenance are scheduled for critical equipment to prevent leaks, malfunctions, and ensure compliance.
Employee Training: Comprehensive training programs on environmental policies, spill prevention, and emergency response procedures are provided to all relevant staff.
Emission Reporting: Emission levels are documented in compliance reports submitted to regulatory authorities, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Process Enclosures: Dust-generating processes, such as cutting and weaving, are enclosed to contain particulate emissions and prevent airborne pollutants from spreading.
Housekeeping: Work areas are maintained with industrial vacuum systems, reducing particulate buildup and supporting clean air quality.
Dust Collection Systems: Dedicated dust collection systems are installed at key points to capture particulates before they disperse, minimizing workplace pollution.

Activated Carbon Filters: Carbon filters are installed in exhaust systems to capture and neutralize volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced during dyeing and finishing.
Low-VOC Materials: Whenever feasible, Gloster uses low-VOC dyes, adhesives, and solvents in manufacturing processes to reduce VOC emissions and ensure safer working conditions.
Ventilation System Checks: Regular inspections are conducted on ventilation systems to ensure they efficiently remove gaseous emissions from the workspace.

Closed-Loop Absorption: Enclosure systems are used to maintain a closed-loop sulfur absorption process, particularly in finishing treatments. These systems help contain emissions and improve air quality.
Regular Monitoring: The sulfur absorption system is monitored daily to verify optimal performance and prevent excess emissions.
Effluent Testing: Routine effluent tests are conducted to ensure sulfur levels in discharge meet regulatory standards, preventing environmental contamination.

Sound Barriers: High-decibel equipment is fitted with sound barriers to reduce noise pollution and maintain a safe noise level for workers.
Operational Scheduling: Noisy operations are scheduled during daytime hours to minimize impact on surrounding communities.
Noise Monitoring: Monthly noise assessments are conducted in high-noise areas to ensure adherence to regulatory noise levels.
Protective Equipment for Workers: Ear protection gear is provided to employees working in high-noise zones to reduce exposure to harmful sound levels.

Activated Carbon Filters: Filters are installed in exhaust systems to capture and neutralize odorous compounds emitted during production.
Storage of Odorous Materials: Materials that may emit odors are stored in sealed containers in well-ventilated areas, reducing odor levels in the workspace and community.
Odor Source Inspection: Routine checks are carried out to identify and control any additional odor sources, helping maintain a pleasant working environment.

Optimized Delivery Scheduling: Delivery and dispatch are scheduled during off-peak hours to prevent traffic congestion and reduce emissions.
Route Planning: Efficient routes are planned for company vehicles to avoid congested areas, ensuring reduced travel times and lower emissions.
Vehicle Maintenance: All company vehicles are regularly maintained to ensure fuel efficiency and minimized emissions, aligning with Gloster’s carbon footprint reduction goals.

Gloster Limited is committed to sustainable water management to reduce consumption, recycle resources, and mitigate environmental impacts. This SOP defines protocols for water recycling, water-saving technologies, wastewater treatment, rainwater harvesting, and risk assessments to enhance operational efficiency and ensure compliance with environmental standards.

sections.title: Water Management Protocols Implemented at Gloster

steps.heading: Technologies for Water Recycling and Reuse

body.text: We have installed advanced closed-loop recycling systems that enable us to reuse water multiple times, significantly reducing freshwater demand.

Reverse Osmosis Systems: Our RO systems treat wastewater to remove contaminants, enabling reuse in non-critical processes such as machine cooling and floor washing.
Effluent Recycling Units: Treated effluents are reused in production, achieving a 20-30% reduction in overall water consumption annually.
Reuse of Condensate Water: Steam condensate from boilers is captured and recycled, reducing the need for additional water intake.
Data Logging and Monitoring: We maintain daily water consumption logs and conduct monthly performance reviews to identify further areas for water-saving improvements.
Employee Engagement: We encourage employees to participate in continuous improvement programs focused on optimizing water reuse through better operational practices.

steps.heading: Adoption of Waterless or Water-Saving Dyeing Technologies

body.text: We have implemented low liquor ratio dyeing machines, enabling us to dye fabrics using minimal water.

Waterless Dyeing Pilot Programs: We are experimenting with supercritical CO2 dyeing technologies that use no water, with promising results in reducing resource consumption.
Air-Dyeing Methods: We are in the process of installing air-dyeing systems that allow dyes to bond with fabric without water.
Digital Printing Adoption: Digital printing methods significantly reduce water usage, as they avoid the need for pre-treatment and post-wash processes typical of conventional dyeing.
Chemical-Free Dye Innovations: We are collaborating with research institutes to develop biodegradable dyes that reduce chemical pollutants and require less rinsing during production.
Annual Dyeing Technology Assessments: These evaluations ensure we remain up-to-date with the latest water-saving innovations and assess scalability for larger production volumes.

steps.heading: Reduction of Water Consumption in Washing and Cleaning Processes

body.text: We have deployed automated washing systems that use water-efficient cycles, optimizing every wash to minimize waste.

Steam Cleaning: Steam-based cleaning technologies have replaced traditional water-intensive washing wherever possible, especially in equipment maintenance.
Trigger-Controlled Hoses: All cleaning staff use trigger-operated hoses to control water flow and prevent unnecessary wastage.
Cleaning Schedule Optimization: High-frequency cleaning areas, such as production floors, have been shifted to weekly cycles, supported by intermediate dry cleaning techniques.
Non-Water Cleaning Agents: For machine parts, we use bio-degradable, non-water solvents that eliminate the need for rinsing with water.
Employee Training on Water Efficiency: Annual training programs are conducted, focusing on low-water cleaning techniques and machine-specific cleaning protocols to reduce water usage by at least 10% annually.
To mitigate operational risks, we conduct comprehensive water risk assessments at multiple levels.

Quarterly Risk Audits: Water risk assessments are carried out every quarter to identify vulnerabilities such as droughts, groundwater depletion, and local water regulations.
Water Footprint Analysis: We evaluate the water footprint of each production stage to identify processes with the highest consumption and implement targeted reduction strategies.
Community Impact Assessments: Collaboration with local authorities ensures that our operations do not negatively impact community water access.
Seasonal Water Contingency Planning: We create water conservation plans for the dry season, including stockpiling treated water and reducing non-essential usage during critical periods.
Third-Party Risk Audits: We engage independent auditors annually to validate our water-related risk assessments and recommend improvements.
Ensuring the quality of discharged water is a critical component of our environmental responsibility.

Onsite Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs): We operate fully compliant WWTPs that treat effluents to meet local environmental standards.
Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) Targets: We are working towards ZLD compliance, ensuring that all wastewater is treated and reused within the facility.
Monthly Water Quality Tests: Samples from treated effluent are analyzed every month for parameters such as Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) to meet environmental norms.
Sludge Treatment: Sludge generated from WWTPs is treated to reduce toxicity and then safely disposed of or repurposed as agricultural compost.
Independent Wastewater Audits: Annual third-party assessments ensure that our wastewater systems comply with evolving environmental regulations and identify areas for further improvement.

steps.heading: Water Accounting and Internal Water Audit

body.text: Gloster Limited has established a formal water accounting and internal water audit mechanism to verify the implementation and effectiveness of its water management initiatives.

Water intake, consumption, reuse, and discharge are measured using installed water meters and operational monitoring systems at key locations.
Water consumption data is recorded on a daily basis and consolidated into monthly water accounting records by the Environmental / Utility team.
An annual water balance statement is prepared to assess total water withdrawal, recycled water usage, wastewater generation, and efficiency improvements.
Water accounting records are reviewed to identify high-consumption areas, abnormal trends, and opportunities for water reduction.

Internal water audits are conducted at least once every year or whenever there are significant process or operational changes.
The water audit includes:
Verification of water accounting data and meter records
Review of water-intensive processes and utilities
Assessment of water recycling, reuse, and rainwater harvesting systems
Evaluation of compliance with internal SOPs and applicable environmental regulations
Audit findings are documented in internal water audit reports or review notes and communicated to plant management for action.

Improvement actions arising from water audits and water accounting reviews are formally documented.
Responsibilities and timelines are assigned to relevant departments.
Implementation status is monitored during periodic environmental and management reviews to ensure effectiveness.

Water accounting data, audit records, and corrective action documentation are maintained as controlled records.
These records are made available for regulatory inspections, customer audits, and ESG / sustainability assessments.
To supplement our water needs, we have installed rainwater harvesting system at all our facilities.

Roof-Mounted Collection Systems: Rainwater is collected from roofs and stored in dedicated underground tanks with a storage capacity of up to 50,000 liters.
Pre-Filtration Systems: Before storage, rainwater passes through first-flush diverters and sediment filters, ensuring that only clean water enters the tanks.
Irrigation and Non-Potable Usage: Harvested rainwater is primarily used for landscaping irrigation, cooling systems, and cleaning outdoor areas.
Bi-Annual Maintenance: The rainwater harvesting infrastructure is inspected twice a year, focusing on filter cleaning, tank desilting, and pump maintenance to ensure optimal performance.
Integration with Water Management System: Rainwater data is logged and reviewed alongside other water metrics to monitor overall efficiency and identify opportunities to further reduce reliance on municipal water supplies.

Real-Time Monitoring Systems: Water consumption and recycling rates are tracked in real time using automated sensors connected to a centralized data system.
Monthly Reports: Water use, recycling levels, and wastewater test results are documented in monthly reports submitted to senior management for review.
Annual Environmental Impact Reports: Our water management efforts are included in annual sustainability reports, which are shared with stakeholders and regulatory authorities.
Incident Reporting Protocols: Any incidents involving water contamination or unexpected disruptions are reported within 24 hours, followed by an investigation and corrective action.

blocks.text: Reuse and Recovery:

In our manufacturing facility, we prioritize the reuse and recovery of furniture and equipment. For instance, when a piece of office furniture is damaged, it is repaired rather than discarded. If the equipment is no longer functional, its components are salvaged and reused in new products, minimizing waste.
Materials such as fabric offcuts and remnants from production processes are not thrown away. Instead, they are repurposed into smaller products, like recycled fabric bags, or sold to partners who specialize in fabric recovery and reuse.
Large fabric rolls that are no longer needed for production are donated to local charities or sold to organizations focused on upcycling materials.
Waste Sorting categories:

All waste must be sorted into distinct categories, including wood, electronic waste (e-waste), electrical wires, scrap metals, glass, and plastics.
E-waste, such as components from old machines, is to be separated and designated for specialized recycling.
Scrap metal waste will be collected and sent to certified metal recycling facilities, where it will be melted down and reused in the manufacturing process.
Waste Sorting Bins:

Waste sorting bins are to be clearly labeled according to the material type: wood, e-waste, electrical wiring, scrap metals, glass, and plastics.
Wood: Brown bin
E-waste: Yellow bin
Electrical Wiring: Blue bin
Scrap Metals: Green bin
Glass: Clear or Transparent bin
Plastics: Red bin
All employees must be trained regularly to ensure proper sorting of waste into the correct bins.
Electronic Waste Handling:

Any electronic components that are no longer functional must be dismantled, with parts like circuit boards, batteries, and metals separated for recycling.
These parts must be sent to certified e-waste recycling centers that adhere to environmental standards for responsible processing.
Metal, Glass, and Plastic Sorting:

Scrap metal will be sent to a certified metal recycling facility where it will be melted down and repurposed.
Glass and plastics are to be sorted separately and delivered to specialized recycling plants where they will be processed into new materials.

sops.title: Hazardous Waste Management and Disposal Procedure

blocks.text: The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to outline the protocols and procedures for the safe labelling, storage, handling, and transportation of hazardous substances at Gloster. This SOP aims to minimize the risk of exposure to hazardous materials, ensure compliance with environmental regulations, and protect the health and safety of employees and the surrounding community.

steps.heading: Use of alternatives and Less Hazardous Substances

substeps.text: To reduce exposure risks, we have replaced traditional solvents with water-based alternatives in our cleaning processes, which are less harmful to both employees and the environment.
Evaluate hazardous substances used in processes and identify less harmful alternatives that fulfill operational requirements.
Gradually replace high-risk substances with less hazardous options to reduce potential health and environmental risks.
In dyeing, we transitioned from chemical dyes to low-impact natural dyes derived from plant sources, which significantly reduced our hazardous waste output.
Consult with industry experts and regulatory bodies to stay informed on emerging safer alternatives and best practices in hazardous substance management.
Document and monitor the impact of reduced-hazard replacements to assess both safety improvements and any operational adjustments needed.
Conduct risk assessments for all hazardous substances, identifying where lower-risk materials could achieve similar results without compromising quality.
After assessing the use of certain solvents, we replaced high-VOC chemicals with less volatile alternatives in our coating process, which has improved air quality in our facilities.
Develop a phased approach to substitute or reduce usage of highly hazardous substances, setting realistic timelines to manage implementation effectively.
Monitor employee exposure levels and provide additional training on the safe handling of less hazardous alternatives to ensure workplace safety is maintained during transitions.
In collaboration with suppliers, we sourced eco-friendly alternatives to traditional flame retardants, which comply with safety regulations while being less toxic.

steps.heading: Minimization of Material Use through Process Enhancement

substeps.text: Process Streamlining: Regularly evaluate manufacturing processes to identify inefficiencies and reduce excessive material consumption.
Analyze production stages to find areas of overuse or wastage of hazardous materials.
Implement advanced dyeing technologies that adapt based on real-time data to minimize dye and solvent use.
Utilize process simulations to test modifications, ensuring both economic and environmental benefits.
Continuously monitor and adapt processes to maintain optimal performance.
Lean Manufacturing Principles: Use Value Stream Mapping (VSM) to identify and eliminate non-value-added activities, thus minimizing hazardous material usage.
Train teams in lean techniques, encouraging a culture of continuous improvement for efficiency suggestions.
Introduce Just-in-Time (JIT) practices to align material use with production needs, reducing excess inventory.
Conserve hazardous materials through lean principles, enhancing productivity and sustainability.
Material Recovery Initiatives: Actively incorporate recovered input materials into production to support sustainability.
Identify opportunities to replace virgin hazardous materials with recovered options, lowering resource extraction and environmental impact.
Conduct regular audits to assess feasibility and quality of recycled or reclaimed materials, such as recycled fabrics.
Integrate these materials to reduce waste and contribute to a circular economy.
Supplier Partnerships: Collaborate with suppliers for high-quality recovered materials that meet quality and safety standards.
Engage suppliers specializing in sustainable recovery to align with our quality and environmental goals.
Build responsible supply chains that reinforce our sustainability practices.

steps.heading: Adoption of Sustainable or Bio-Based Raw Materials

substeps.text: Sustainable Material Sourcing: Transition to eco-friendly, bio-based materials with lower environmental risks.
Research sustainable alternatives with reduced harm to human health and the environment.
Prioritize certified eco-friendly materials, such as organic cotton, to achieve sustainability goals.
Research and Development: Invest in R&D to explore alternative, eco-friendly materials and collaborate with institutions for innovation.
Test and validate bio-based materials to ensure performance and sustainability from production to disposal.

Standardized Labeling: In our chemical storage area, we use Globally Harmonized System (GHS) labels on all containers, such as hazard symbols indicating corrosive or flammable substances. This system helps us align with international safety standards and ensures consistent labeling across all sites.

Language and Clarity: For our production facility in France, all chemical labels are printed in both French and English. This ensures that our international team members, including those who speak English as a second language, can fully understand the hazards and safety precautions.
Regular Inspections: Conduct monthly label inspections to ensure intact, legible, and accurate labeling.

Dedicated Storage Areas: In our chemical storage facility, we maintain separate, ventilated storage areas for flammable and corrosive chemicals. These areas are equipped with fire suppression systems, and access is restricted to trained personnel only. Every three months, our safety officer conducts compliance assessments to ensure that all storage protocols are followed, and no incompatible materials are stored together.

Secondary Containment: At our manufacturing plant, we have installed spill pallets and bunds under chemical storage tanks to contain any accidental spills. For example, our solvent storage area includes custom spill containment systems that hold up to 110% of the largest container's volume to prevent environmental contamination in case of leaks.

Environmental Controls: Our hazardous material storage room in the warehouse is monitored with temperature and humidity controls. We use automated sensors that send alerts if conditions exceed safe levels, ensuring substances are stored under the optimal conditions to maintain their stability.

Inventory Management: We use a digital inventory management system to track all hazardous substances in our warehouse. Every 30 days, we perform an inventory check to update the system and verify that all materials are accounted for and safely stored.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): In our lab and persons who exposure with hazardous substance, all workers handling chemicals are required to wear gloves, goggles, and respirators. PPE is inspected weekly to ensure that it is in good condition. For instance, we recently replaced all worn gloves in the chemical mixing area after a routine inspection.

Training Programs: Our safety training program includes an annual session on handling hazardous substances, which is mandatory for all new hires and existing staff. The training covers proper techniques for handling, spill responses, and emergency procedures for exposure.

Controlled Handling Areas: In our production facility, we have designated areas for handling hazardous substances, such as chemical mixing zones, where proper ventilation systems and spill containment trays are installed. Only authorized personnel are allowed to operate in these areas, ensuring that all handling complies with safety protocols.

Certified Transport Vehicles: We utilize certified vehicles equipped with spill kits, fire extinguishers, and appropriate signage for transporting hazardous chemicals. For instance, our trucks used for transporting flammable liquids are regularly inspected every 15 days to ensure they meet safety standards.

Driver Training: All drivers responsible for transporting hazardous substances undergo training on safe handling, emergency spill response, and fire safety. Every six months, they attend a refresher course that covers updated safety regulations and emergency response techniques.

Documentation: For each hazardous shipment, we ensure that all drivers carry a complete set of documents, including Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), transport manifests, and emergency contact information. These documents are checked before departure to ensure compliance with legal and safety requirements.

Route Planning: When planning transportation routes for hazardous substances, we avoid densely populated areas and environmentally sensitive zones. We use GIS mapping to identify alternative routes that minimize risk and potential exposure in case of an accident.

steps.heading: Specialized Treatment and Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

substeps.text: Waste Segregation: In our production facility, we strictly separate hazardous and non-hazardous waste. For example, we use color-coded bins: red for hazardous materials and green for non-hazardous waste. This segregation is reviewed every two months to ensure compliance with local regulations and reduce cross-contamination risks.Separate hazardous from non-hazardous waste with proper labeling, reviewed every 2 months.

Neutralization and Treatment: Before disposing of certain hazardous chemicals, such as acids, we apply neutralization processes to reduce their toxicity. For example, our team neutralizes waste sulfuric acid using a neutralizing agent before disposal, significantly reducing environmental impact.

Waste Minimization: In our production process, we continuously strive to minimize hazardous waste by optimizing materials. For instance, we've switched to using water-based solvents instead of organic solvents, reducing the volume of hazardous waste generated.

Documentation and Reporting: We maintain monthly records of all hazardous waste disposal activities. For instance, after disposing of waste chemical containers, we generate detailed reports that include quantities, disposal methods, and certificates of destruction, which are kept in our compliance database for auditing purposes.

They are a certified waste management provider specializing in handling and treating hazardous materials. Through this collaboration, we ensure that all hazardous waste is properly collected, treated, and disposed of in compliance with environmental regulations.

sops.title: Employee Performance evaluation system and career development plan

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines structured guidelines for assessing employee performance at Ananya Jute Mills. This approach focuses on quantitatively and qualitatively evaluating each employee’s contribution within the jute manufacturing process, identifying improvement areas, offering development support, and recognizing outstanding performance in line with our industry standards.

This SOP applies to all employees, including production teams, maintenance crews, quality control, administrative staff, and management at Ananya. It covers all performance evaluations conducted within the organization, particularly focusing on job roles and responsibilities specific to jute manufacturing operations.

body.text: 3.1.1 Performance Criteria: Define relevant performance criteria based on job roles, specific responsibilities, and organizational goals within the jute manufacturing context. Criteria may include:

Quality of output specific to jute processing standards.
Productivity and efficiency in the manufacturing line.
Adherence to safety protocols in the factory environment.
Team collaboration and communication, particularly in production workflows.
Problem-solving abilities relevant to jute production challenges and machinery operation.
3.1.2 Evaluation Metrics: Use metrics tailored to the manufacturing industry to provide a balanced view of performance. Examples include:

Quantitative: Number of jute rolls processed, defect rates in finished products, attendance and punctuality records.
Qualitative: Feedback from supervisors on handling of jute fiber, team-based reviews on productivity, self-assessment insights.

3.2.1 Frequency of Assessments: Schedule formal evaluations bi-annually to provide comprehensive feedback on employee performance. Conduct informal check-ins quarterly to discuss ongoing progress, address challenges in production, and offer support where needed.
3.2.2 Evaluation Methods: Self-Assessment: Encourage employees to complete a self-assessment form that reflects on their contribution to jute manufacturing standards and safety practices.
Supervisor Assessment: Supervisors will assess employees based on specific observations, performance data, and their adherence to production standards, providing feedback that is both practical and actionable.
Peer Review: Implement a peer review process where team members share constructive insights on each other’s work quality and adherence to production protocols, fostering a collaborative work culture.

3.3.1 Performance Review Meetings: Hold a formal review meeting to discuss the evaluation results. Supervisors and employees will discuss areas of strength, opportunities for improvement, and necessary development steps, particularly focusing on production quality and safety compliance.

3.3.2 Goal Setting: Collaboratively establish SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) goals for the next assessment period, directly connected to jute production efficiency and quality standards.

sops.title: SOP for Ethical Compliance Due Diligence Program for Third Parties

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines a structured framework for implementing an Ethical Compliance Due Diligence Program for third parties associated with Ananya Jute Mills. This program aims to ensure that third-party entities align with our standards in areas such as anti-corruption, labor practices, environmental responsibility, data privacy, human rights, and health and safety, reducing risks linked to unethical practices.

This SOP applies to all third-party engagements at Ananya Jute Mills, including suppliers, vendors, commission agents, brokers, sales representatives, distributors, contractors, customs brokers, and consultants. It is relevant across all departments interacting with third parties to uphold ethical, legal, and regulatory compliance.

body.text: Initial Background Check: Conduct background checks on potential third parties to identify ethical risks, focusing on the following:

Anti-Corruption and Bribery: Verify compliance with anti-bribery laws and third-party policies.
Labor Practices: Confirm fair labor standards adherence, ensuring no history of child or forced labor.
Environmental Responsibility: Review practices for sustainability alignment and environmental protection.
Data Privacy and Information Security: Ensure compliance with information security standards.
Human Rights and Fair Treatment: Confirm commitment to human rights, diversity, and equity.
Health and Safety: Verify adherence to workplace health and safety protocols.
Assessment of Ethical Areas: The Compliance and Risk Management Team evaluates third-party practices, focusing on:

Anti-Corruption Compliance: Reviewing adherence to anti-bribery laws.
Labor and Human Rights: Ensuring alignment with fair labor and human rights practices.
Environmental Responsibility: Assessing environmental practices to support sustainability objectives.
Data Privacy / Information security: Reviewing data handling protocols to protect sensitive company and client information.
Health and Safety Compliance: Confirming compliance with safety standards.
Data Collection and Benchmarking:

Data Collection: Gather relevant documents, such as certifications and policies on labor and environmental standards.
Benchmarking: Compare third-party practices to industry standards within the jute manufacturing sector.
Required Documentation: Review the following to confirm compliance:

Anti-Corruption and Labor Policies: Documents on ethical practices, labor standards, and anti-bribery.
Environmental Certifications: Relevant certifications showing alignment with environmental standards.
Data Privacy and Security Certifications: ISO 27001 or equivalent certifications for information security.
Human Rights and Health Standards: Documentation on human rights and safety standards.
Ethical Risk Evaluation: Assess potential risks based on third-party data access, practices, and compliance records.

Corruption Risks: Check the reputation and ethical track record.
Data Security Risks: Review the third-party’s data security policies and compliance history.
Approval by Senior Management: Findings from the risk assessment guide final decisions. Approval from senior management, including Compliance and IT Security Officers, is required before engagement.
Approval Documentation: Record the approval process to ensure transparency.
Third parties are classified based on corruption and information security risk prior to engagement:

Low Risk: Standard suppliers with no government interaction and no access to sensitive data
Medium Risk: Vendors with limited data access or service-based contracts
High Risk: Commission agents, customs brokers, consultants, IT vendors, distributors, or any third party interacting with government authorities or handling sensitive company data
For all third parties, and especially high-risk third parties, the following anti-corruption checks are conducted:

Verification of ownership, management structure, and business reputation
Screening for past legal, regulatory, or corruption-related violations
Disclosure of any government affiliations or politically exposed persons (PEPs)
Review of commission structures, incentives, and payment terms
Confirmation of acceptance of Ananya Jute Mills’ Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption requirements
All third-party contracts include anti-corruption clauses, audit rights, and termination rights for non-compliance.
Information security due diligence is conducted for third parties that access, process, or store Company information. Controls include:

Completion of an information security assessment or questionnaire
Evaluation of data protection measures, access controls, and incident response capabilities
Classification of data access (low, medium, high sensitivity)
Approval of system or data access by IT Security prior to engagement
Contractual obligations covering confidentiality, data protection, and breach notification
Access rights are reviewed periodically and revoked upon contract completion or termination.

Scheduled Audits and Assessments: Ananya Jute Mills will conduct an on-site audit at least once a year for each third-party supplier to evaluate their compliance across key parameters, including anti-corruption measures, IT security, health and safety protocols, environmental impact, and social responsibility, among other criteria.

Additionally, all suppliers are required to complete a self-assessment annually to verify their adherence to these standards and maintain transparency.

Incident Reporting: Third parties must immediately report any breaches in ethical standards or safety protocols.

Regular Communication: Engage regularly with third parties to address compliance concerns and operational updates.

Reporting Protocols: Require immediate reporting of any incidents or breaches in ethical standards, data security, or safety by third parties.

Response Planning: Collaborate on incident response plans that outline roles, responsibilities, and procedures for managing ethical or data-related incidents.

blocks.text:
Documentation Maintenance: Maintain records of due diligence activities, risk assessments, approvals, and communications.

Record Retention: Retain records for a minimum of three years to support accountability and traceability in compliance activities.

narrative.text:
Audits and Inspections: Conduct regular audits to confirm compliance with this SOP and identify potential improvement areas.

Compliance Manager’s Responsibility: The Compliance Manager oversees due diligence practices and ensures adherence to this SOP.

blocks.text:
Adherence Requirement: All employees and third parties must comply with this SOP. Non-compliance may lead to corrective actions or termination of engagement.

Regulatory Compliance: Ananya Jute Mills – Gloster Limited will adhere to applicable local, national, and international ethical and regulatory standards.

responsibilities: Ensure SOP implementation and enforcement, providing necessary resources for training and compliance.
Oversee monitoring, conduct training, and review this SOP periodically.
Follow all guidelines and report any ethical or compliance concerns to the Compliance Manager.

blocks.text: Review Period: This SOP will be reviewed and updated every two years or as needed based on regulatory or operational changes.

The internal assessment SOP aligns with the planned arrangements, meeting the requirements of the relevant standards and the internal management system policies of the organization.
This procedure covers the complete documented consumer product management system, including the internal audit process, within its scope.

responsibilities: Holds the primary responsibility for implementing and maintaining this procedure.
Supported by qualified internal auditors in carrying out this task.

blocks.text: The Chief Internal Auditor holds the primary responsibility for implementing and maintaining this procedure. They will be supported by qualified internal auditors in carrying out this task.

rows.definition: A situation where specified requirements are not fulfilled.
A major failure to meet safety or legal compliance.
A substantial failure to meet any standard requirement or a scenario that raises significant doubt about the conformity of the product based on available objective evidence.
A failure to meet specific requirements, where conformity of the product remains in doubt based on objective evidence.

body.text: The Chief Internal Auditor will create an Internal Audit Plan based on the following considerations:

The significance and status of operations related to the consumer product management system.
The importance of operations related to product safety, legality, and quality.
Results from prior audits.
Regular internal assessments on ESG issues including air pollution, health and safety, working conditions, child labor, forced labor and human trafficking, corruption, information security, employee satisfaction surveys, and other relevant ESG factors.
An Internal Audit Schedule will be created according to the frequency specified in the Internal Audit Plan and will be shared with all relevant parties.
Internal audits will be performed by qualified internal auditors who are independent of the activities being examined. A List of Internal Auditors will be maintained by the Chief of Internal Audit.
Before conducting an audit, internal auditors will prepare an Internal Audit Checklist cum Observation Sheet , consulting the following:

Hazards and risks associated with the operations.
Relevant industry standards (e.g., BRC Standard).
Previous audit checklists and nonconformity reports, if applicable.
During the audit, internal auditors will document observations against each checklist item. Any nonconformities identified will be recorded in the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report.

The auditor will review the Quality Assurance Plan to ensure it aligns with actual practices. They will also evaluate quality-related facilities such as designated quality checking areas, lighting, and waste disposal facilities. Any required modifications will be noted in the audit observation sheet.
Mechanical tools, machines, and tool management on the production floor will be checked, including the list of tools and their integrity.

Internal auditors are responsible for verifying control samples on the production floor and comparing them with the tamper-proof prototypes kept in secure storage. Any discrepancies will be documented.

The list of measuring and monitoring devices used in quality assurance procedures will be reviewed, and their calibration status will be verified against the master calibration list. Any devices not in use should be noted in the master list with reasons for their exclusion.

During the site audit, the auditor will verify that identification markings for semi-finished and finished goods are present, ensuring traceability is maintained. Missing marks will be noted during the site tour.
The internal audit will also assess the lighting conditions and ensure that they meet the standard requirements as per the most stringent buyer specifications.

Complaints handling will be reviewed to ensure that customer complaints are accurately recorded and resolved. All complaints should be documented with sufficient supporting details and properly closed in the complaint handling register.
To confirm that the most up-to-date documents are being used, the internal auditor will check whether the current versions are in use on the production floor, as documented in controlled documents.

Any corrective actions for identified nonconformities will be discussed and agreed upon by both the auditor and auditee. These actions will be recorded in the internal audit nonconformity report, along with a target completion date.
Once the audit is completed, the internal auditor will submit the Internal Audit Checklist cum Observation Sheet to the Chief Internal Auditor.

The Chief Internal Auditor will coordinate follow-up audits to verify the implementation and effectiveness of corrective and/or preventive actions. The timelines for addressing nonconformities are as follows:

Minor Nonconformities: 60 days
Major Nonconformities: 30 days
Critical Nonconformities: 7 days
The results of follow-up audits will be documented in the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report.
After the follow-up audit, the internal auditor will submit the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report to the Chief of Internal Audit.
The Chief Internal Auditor will prepare and forward the Internal Audit Summary Report for discussion during the Management Review Meeting.
In addition to departmental audits, a separate internal audit will be conducted annually.
